proposal.name: clarify_associations_not_causation_in_comparative_analysis
proposal.trigger: When preparing reports or presentations that present observed differences between groups, segments, or claim characteristics.
proposal.objective: Prevent misinterpretation of observed group differences as causal effects by explicitly documenting that findings represent statistical associations, not causal relationships.
procedure: When your analysis reveals differences in metrics (rates, averages, or distributions) across groups or segments, add the 'association_not_causation' caveat to the report's Caveats section.
In the caveat, explicitly state that observed differences represent statistical associations and do not imply causal mechanisms or causal relationships.
Explain that the descriptive analysis cannot determine whether differences arise from causal effects, confounding variables, or other factors outside the scope of the data.
Place this caveat early in the Caveats section, before results are presented, so readers understand this interpretive limit.
required_checks: Verify that the report includes the 'association_not_causation' caveat either as a listed caveat item or as explicit language in the report text.
Confirm that the caveat language clearly distinguishes between observed statistical associations and causal relationships.
failure_modes: Presenting group differences without clarifying they may not be causal, leading readers to assume causal mechanisms.
Operational decisions made on the false assumption that observed differences represent causal effects.
Over-interpretation of patterns as actionable causal insights rather than descriptive associations.
proposal.example: When an analysis compares denial rates between two segments and observes that one has higher rates, the caveat clarifies that this observed difference is a statistical association and does not establish causality. Other unmeasured factors—such as claim documentation completeness, submission patterns, or case complexity—could contribute to the observed difference.
